source.title: Align-then-Unlearn: Embedding Alignment for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Philipp Spohn; Leander Girrbach; Jessica Bader; Zeynep Akata

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates a new embedding-based unlearning method and reports forgetting, utility, and adversarial-attack-probe results relevant to unlearning robustness.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own Align-then-Unlearn results on RWKU, including adversarial-attack probe scores. It does not report recovery attacks using relearning, activation ablation, or quantization. Prior attack findings in related work are cited, not tested here. The numerical baseline-method results are identified as following the RWKU benchmark and are not extracted as this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (Align-then-Unlearn) for Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct. It reports its own RWKU forget, neighbor and MMLU scores, plus RWKU adversarial-attack (AA) probe scores. These bear on A (forgetting with retained utility), E (prompt-based recovery) and F (a newer method claimed robust to rephrasing). No relearning, activation-ablation or quantization attacks are run, so B, C and D are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that embedding-space unlearning removes target knowledge (forget probe down to 13.5%) with negligible MMLU loss, and is promising for robustness to rephrasing. They also report that it degrades neighboring knowledge, that the threshold τ does not transfer across targets, and that effectiveness depends on layer for individual targets. Robustness to hidden-state attacks is only hypothesized, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The method trains an embedding prediction module and then fine-tunes the model to reduce similarity to a target concept embedding, with iterative realignment; it is not a test of gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU recovery recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The unlearning threshold/checkpoint changes the forgetting–retention trade-off. Layer choice changes results for individual targets; for Warren Buffett the reported forget accuracy is 54.32% at layer 10 and 12.40% at layer 20.
record.peer_reviewed: The International Conference on Machine Learning 2025 Workshop on Machine Unlearning for Generative AI
record.problems: Only Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct is evaluated. The text gives no uncertainty estimates or chance-level reference for the forget scores. The reported AA probe details are not specified here, and some layer and trade-off results are available only as figures.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Numerical baseline-method results are described as following the RWKU benchmark and are not treated as this study's own results.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack; this is cited only (Hu et al. 2025).
No activation ablation or steering attack, and no analysis of deletion versus blocked access. The authors only hypothesize robustness to hidden-state attacks.
No quantization attack; this is cited only (Zhang et al. 2024b).
The AA probes are not broken down into rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context types. No sampling-based decoding attack is run.
Robustness is shown only against RWKU AA prompting probes, not against fine-tuning, internal-edit or quantization attacks.
Only one model is tested. No WMDP or Harry Potter settings. No chance reference is given for open-ended forget probes.

missing.what: Third Table 1 column for ATU (48.8/37.2/25.9 vs 55.8 before unlearning). This is likely Forget AA (or another forget probe) under RWKU's standard six-column order, and no row captures it. The column identities of the first three columns need checking against the RWKU layout.

Baseline-method rows (GA, NPO, DPO, ICU, RT) taken from the RWKU benchmark. The AA column for these could show prompting recovery for older methods, but these are cited RWKU numbers, correctly left out as the study's own results.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 text extraction is garbled: the header lists QA/AA under Forget, but there are six numeric columns. The prose calls 13.5 'Forget QA', which conflicts with RWKU's usual FB/QA/AA order. The reader mixed columns in the neighbor rows (baseline 55.8 is the third column, values come from the fourth and fifth), and these have been corrected. Per-version state for r2/r7/r12: E absent, F observed. This is a workshop paper with a single model and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not state a chance-level reference for the reported forget accuracies. Its results are for one model and do not separately test every unlearning method named in the claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is run.
No activation-direction ablation or recovery test is run; the study does not experimentally distinguish deletion from blocked access.
The study reports RWKU adversarial-attack probe scores, but does not specify separate results for rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The proposed method is evaluated on RWKU adversarial-attack probes, but not against the fine-tuning, internal-edit, or quantization attacks named in the claim.
